chunk_findings.detail: `acquire` reserves `need` slots by calling `Slots.hold` once per slot, so a lane can hold a partial set of slots while it waits for the rest. With a GPU pool of `limit=2`, two concurrent lanes using task resource `gpu:2` (`need=2`) and `timeout_s=None` can take different one-slot locks (e.g. slot 0 and slot 1), then each block forever in its second `hold`, waiting for the slot held by the other. The pool-name ordering only orders different pools; it does not make multi-slot acquisition within one pool atomic, and the scheduler’s `busy_counts`/`refusals` are stale before the race reaches `acquire`. The same partial-hold behavior also lets a lane hold slots in an earlier pool while waiting for a later pool, blocking other lanes that need only the earlier pool. This contradicts the stated no-lease/no-hold-while-waiting behavior and violates [r-lock-cycle-selfheal].
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/capacity.py:acquire

chunk_findings.detail: The source-text guard intended to enforce “no lease” is ineffective. It only rejects the literal substrings `"import lease"` and `"from .. import lease"`, but a module in `ddflow/services/lanes` can import the lease service as `from ..lease import acquire` (or `import ddflow.services.lease`), and none of those banned substrings appear. Given such a `capacity.py`, the test passes even though capacity may acquire leases while waiting, directly violating [r-lock-cycle-selfheal].
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_capacity.py:test_wait_holds_no_lease_and_is_bounded

chunk_findings.detail: The test claims to verify that a waiting lane holds no lease, but it only checks that the directory contains `ep-local.0.lock`. Lock files remain after release, so this assertion does not prove the slot is free. If `C.acquire` locks `ep-local.0.lock`, times out, and leaves the lock file descriptor open, the directory still contains exactly `ep-local.0.lock` and the test passes, while `C.busy_counts(pools, tmp_path)` would report `{"ep-local": 1}`. The test should assert zero busy count after the outer holder exits; otherwise a leaked lease can pass.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_capacity.py:test_wait_holds_no_lease_and_is_bounded

chunk_findings.detail: The change explicitly implements waiting as a poll: it adds `import time` and documents that “the wait is a bounded poll of the caller’s own process, `timeout_s` long.” This violates [r-lock-cycle-selfheal], which says agents never poll-wait or hold while waiting. A lane calling `capacity.acquire` on a full endpoint/GPU pool will still poll/sleep until the timeout, even if it holds no lease; satisfying the “no lease” half of the rule does not remove the prohibited poll-wait.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/capacity.py: module docstring / acquire wait

chunk_findings.detail: Finite `timeout_s` is not enforced as a hard deadline. After a failed sweep the code checks the deadline, then unconditionally sleeps `poll_s`, then retries; if that retry succeeds it yields instead of timing out. For example, with `timeout_s=0.01`, `poll_s=1.0`, and a pool occupied on the first sweep but free on the next, the loop misses, sees the deadline not yet reached, sleeps past the deadline, succeeds on the next sweep, and returns `Held(..., waited_s≈1.0)`. The documented contract “SlotsTimeout when they are not all free after timeout_s” is violated, and a scheduler relying on the timeout can launch a lane after its allowed wait.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/capacity.py:acquire

chunk_findings.detail: When a sweep misses, `_try_all` discards which pool caused the miss, and the timeout branch always raises for `ordered[0]`. Given two pools `a` and `b` with `a` free and `b` occupied, `timeout_s=0`, `_try_all` takes `a`, fails on `b`, releases `a`, returns `None`, and the timeout branch raises `SlotsTimeout("a", <limit of a>, 0.0)`. The exception names and limits the wrong pool, and it also reports `timeout_s` as the waited time rather than the measured wait, so any scheduler or baseline that uses the exception to identify the saturated pool receives incorrect data.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/capacity.py:acquire

chunk_findings.detail: The test does not actually exercise a lane that is waiting. It calls `C.acquire(pools, 0, tmp_path)` with `timeout_s=0`, so it only covers the immediate-failure path. A `capacity.acquire` implementation that still holds the first free GPU slot while waiting for the second (the prior deadlock scenario with `timeout_s=None`) would pass this test: with timeout `0` it can take one slot, fail to take the other, release the first, and `busy_counts` would still show only the external holder’s one slot. Therefore the test cannot verify the “holds NOTHING meanwhile” property or the two-lane interleaving described in its docstring, leaving the [r-lock-cycle-selfheal] requirement untested.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_capacity.py:test_no_hold_while_waiting_two_gpu_lanes

chunk_findings.detail: `headroom_term` does not compute the “smallest free share among the pools” its docstring promises. It computes `(h.free - h.need + 1) / h.limit` instead of a free-slot share. For an idle 2-slot GPU pool that needs 2 slots (`Headroom("gpu", 2, 0, 2)`), the free share is `1.0` because all 2 of 2 slots are free, but this returns `(2 - 2 + 1) / 2 == 0.5`; for `busy=1` on the same pool it returns `0.0` even though the pool is not full. Every `need > 1` pool therefore feeds SW-headroom an artificially low headroom value, so the swarm baseline will treat an empty multi-slot GPU as partly busy.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/capacity.py:headroom_term

chunk_findings.detail: The change still codifies a poll-wait. The test expects `C.acquire(pools, 30, tmp_path, sleep=sleep, poll_s=0.01)` to call `sleep` and retry when a slot is full, i.e. the lane's process sits in a bounded poll loop. This violates [r-lock-cycle-selfheal], whose record says agents never poll-wait or hold while waiting. The prior triage's suitelock docstring probe does not answer this: that docstring is not the rule record and cannot add an exception the rule does not contain.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_lane_capacity.py:test_wait_succeeds_when_slot_frees

chunk_findings.detail: The source-text guard rejects valid capacity code. `banned in src.split('"""', 2)[2].replace("# lease", "")` treats the substring `"lease"` as forbidden, but `"lease"` is also inside ordinary words such as `"release"`. A correct `capacity.py` that defines a `release(held)` helper, or mentions “released” in a comment after the module docstring, would fail this test even though the waiting lane holds no lease. The test is enforcing an implementation spelling, not the behavior it claims.

chunk_findings.detail: Still present: `acquire` is a bounded poll-wait loop. It repeatedly calls `_try_all`, and on a miss calls `sleep(...)` and retries until `timeout_s`. This violates [r-lock-cycle-selfheal], which states agents never poll-wait; the docstring itself acknowledges “the wait is a bounded poll of the caller's own process.” The all-or-none behavior avoids holding while waiting but does not remove the poll-wait, and a suitelock docstring cannot add an exception the rule does not contain.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/capacity.py:acquire

chunk_findings.detail: `_try_all` calls `stack.close()` on a failed sweep, but that is the same `ExitStack` that `acquire` keeps and reuses on the next poll loop. After `close()`, the next `stack.enter_context(...)` raises `RuntimeError` (“Attempted to enter context on a closed ExitStack”), not `SLOTS.SlotsTimeout`. Concretely: two lanes target the same endpoint with `endpoint_slots=1` and the default `slot_wait_s=600`. The first lane holds the sole slot; the second lane’s first sweep misses, `_try_all` closes the stack, `acquire` sleeps once, then the second sweep raises `RuntimeError` instead of waiting up to the 600 s timeout. The bounded slot wait is therefore broken on the first contention.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/capacity.py:_try_all

chunk_findings.detail: The new capacity wait path is a polling loop: `C.acquire(..., sleep=sleep, poll_s=0.01)` repeatedly invokes `sleep` between checks, and `test_timeout_names_the_full_pool_and_never_overshoots` asserts the poll-sleep/clamp behavior. That is exactly the poll-wait prohibited by the rule that agents never poll-wait or hold while waiting. A lane waiting for a slot will sit in a `time.sleep()` sweep loop rather than blocking on a lock/event and can mask dependency-cycle delays, so the change violates the rule while only testing that the lane holds no lease during the nap.

chunk_findings.detail: `pools_for` clamps every capacity to at least one: `Pool(name, max(1, int(caps.get(name, 1))), need)`. A pool declared with zero slots is treated as one slot. Input `caps={"gpu": 0}`, `resources=["gpu:1"]` produces `Pool("gpu", 1, 1)`, so `refusals` returns no refusal and `acquire` will hold a lane slot for a pool that has zero GPUs. This defeats the hard filter and oversubscribes a zero-capacity resource.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/lanes/capacity.py:pools_for

chunk_findings.detail: For a pool that cannot fit any lane, `lane_figures` returns `cap = max(1, h.limit // need)`, i.e. `1`, not `0`. Input `Headroom("gpu", 1, 0, need=4)` returns `(0, 1)` from `lane_figures`, claiming one lane of capacity although zero lanes fit. This contradicts the function’s own “capacity in lanes” contract and gives SW-score a nonzero capacity for an impossible pool.

chunk_findings.detail: `proc.stdout.readline()` is a blocking read with no timeout. If `C.acquire` in the child process blocks before printing `held`, the parent test blocks forever in `readline()`, and the `finally: proc.kill()` is never reached. Given a `C.acquire` deadlock, this test turns a deterministic regression into an indefinite CI hang.
